title: Fastpath degradation map: batch vs multiplex - notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental notes for an internal collateral slide / one-pager: map how the fastpath (low-latency serving) degrades across three runtime strategies when exposed to conversational microbursts. We want a small, shareable table + ascii charts for product/solutions decks.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Multiplexing (slot-multiplexer that interleaves small requests) reduces p99/p999 tail compared to naive 100ms windowed batching in microburst-heavy sessions, at the cost of slightly higher steady-state p50 and reduced peak qps.
- Windowed batching gives best amortized cost-per-token for sustained throughput but suffers long tails under bursty arrivals (cold/uncached KV sequences).
- Hybrid (prefetch + multiplex fallback) gives a middle ground: most predictable p95, moderate cost.

Experimental setup (notes, approximate):
- Hardware: 8xA100 per pool, same model (llama-13b-like profile), quantized int8 for all experiments.
- Workload: synthetic conversation traces sampled from customer_qa_cohort_12 (approx 30k sessions), mix: 65% short (avg 30 tokens), 25% medium (avg 120 tokens), 10% long (avg 450 tokens). Burst injection: for 3% of sessions inject 0->20 concurrent turns within 400ms.
- Configs compared:
  1) Batched-100ms: windowed batching commit every 100ms, prefix cache ON, no prefetch.
  2) Multiplex-actor: per-session actor multiplexing, opportunistic tiny batches (5-10ms packing), priority headroom preemption for interactive sessions.
  3) Hybrid-prefetch: aggressive prefix prefetch + multiplex fallback after 60ms waiting.
- Measurement: client-observed token latency per generate call; p50/p95/p99/p999 measured, throughput in qps and tokens/s, compute cost extrapolated to $/1M tokens using current pricing model baseline.

Representative numbers (median of 5 runs):
Latency percentiles (ms)
Strategy            | p50  | p95  | p99  | p999 | qps (sustained)
--------------------|------|------|------|------|---------------
Batched-100ms       | 16   | 140  | 420  | 1100 | 640           
Multiplex-actor     | 22   | 88   | 210  | 460  | 510           
Hybrid-prefetch     | 18   | 102  | 240  | 650  | 580           

Cost (extrapolated) - USD per 1M tokens (incl infra + amortized idle)
- Batched-100ms : $39.8
- Multiplex-actor : $34.1
- Hybrid-prefetch : $36.5

Short observations from the numbers:
- Batched config compresses compute (highest qps) so cost/unit is lowest in steady state, but p99/p999 blow up during bursts (see below).
- Multiplexing reduces extreme tails by avoiding head-of-line blocking inside 100ms windows; p95/p99 improved ~2x vs batched. Lower cost per token than batched here due to fewer lost-units and less wasteful overprovisioning in replayed runs (note: this is workload-dependent).
- Hybrid shows the best p95 predictability, with a small cost premium vs multiplex but significantly better experience vs pure batching during mid-size bursts.

Ascii microburst timeline (single 12-request spike) - client observed latency per request (ms):
Time -> 0ms   20ms   40ms   60ms   80ms   100ms  140ms  200ms  400ms
Batched-100ms : 18    22     30     110    380    720    800    980    1100
Multiplex-actor: 24    28     36     46     58     76     112    240    460
Hybrid-prefetch: 20    24     32     68     120    220    320    480    650

Interpretation: batching lumps many triggers to the next window causing a large step function in observed latency; multiplex smooths but increases nominal baseline. Hybrid gives partial smoothing with early-prefetch benefiting a subset.

Chart-style bullets for slides (short):
- Bullets for deck slide 1 (cost vs tail risk):
  * X-axis: cost per 1M tokens (lower better). Y-axis: p99 latency (ms).
  * Batched sits left-bottom for steady-state but extreme up on p99 during spikes -> wide error bar.
  * Multiplex sits slightly right (higher cost) but narrower error bar and lower p99.
  * Hybrid sits center-left with tight p95 and moderate p99.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How sensitive are these results to token length mix? (run quick sweep for +20% long-session mix).
- Does batching with adaptive window (latency-based early flush) close gap vs multiplex? (small experiment planned ENG-1427).
- Impact of KV-cache miss rates: current workload had ~12% cold KV misses; need a cold-heavy run to stress prefetch logic.
- Model size sensitivity: run same profiles on 70B-equivalent (we expect multiplex penalty grows due to larger memory movement).

Recommendations for collateral:
- Produce a 1-slide tradeoff graphic showing steady-state cost vs tail risk with 3 colored markers and error bars (use numbers above). Add a small microburst timeline ascii as the slide notes.
- Include a tiny appendix with the table above and the experiment parameters.
- Call out operational knobs: batching window, multiplex slot size, prefetch horizon. Provide suggested defaults for customer tiers:
  * Free / low-tier: Batched-100ms (cost optimized).
  * Scale / enterprise: Hybrid-prefetch (balanced).
  * Interactive tier / SLO-sensitive: Multiplex-actor (predictability).

Notes to self (informal):

- Might add cost lines for cold-start penalty separately (we're folding it into current numbers but could mislead).
- Add link to raw traces: s3://redwood-test/bench/fastpath-Jun12 (WIP).

- multiplex actor scheduler has two tunables (slot-size and idle-park-time) which we did not sweep.
